key_insight: An attention-fused TFT–N-BEATS model combines short-term dynamics with long-term patterns to forecast photovoltaic power across five horizons.
engineering_relevance: Unified 30-minute to 24-hour forecasts could support grid scheduling and PV–battery operation; the study concerns power forecasting, not perovskite cell design.
method: TFT learns short-term dependencies and dynamic feature importance.
N-BEATS decomposes long-term trends and seasonality.
Adaptive attention fuses both branches for simultaneous multi-horizon prediction.
evidence_signal: On four multi-year DKASC datasets, the abstract reports RMSE values of 42.35–52.29, a 35–40% reduction versus TFT, and MAPE below 5%.
watch_item: RMSE units, horizon-specific errors, and validation beyond DKASC are not specified in the abstract, limiting assessment of operational transferability.
paper_title: A Hybrid TFT-NBEATS Framework for Robust Multi-Horizon Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
